text:
deploy-bot: Deployment v2.3.7 to rl-service (prod us-east-1) finished by hannah. tags: release/channel=canary, feature=exemption-filter

hannah: rolling v2.3.7 out canary -> then prod. this includes the exemptions rewrite (no schema change, just filter ordering). will monitor dashboards.

pagerduty-bot: ALERT -> rl-service: high_429_rate (threshold breached) — paging oncall: @ryan :rotating_light:

ryan: oncall here, seeing paged alert. looking at dashboards now. link: https://monitoring.redwood/internal/dashboards/rl-429-spike

luca: I see a ~7x jump in 429s, 95th latency stable. traces show requests are hitting rate-limiter with exemption check returning false.

jin: quick note — the exemptions change reordered evaluation to run after token accounting in the handler. rolling flag was supposed to be off for prod but looks like it landed on. checking deploy config.

hannah: ugh. in the config PR I toggled `EXEMPTIONS_ORDER=after_accounting` for canary testing; it should have been gated. I must've merged the kube manifest without the guard. :facepalm:

ryan: can someone confirm current env on running pods?

jin: running `kubectl -n rl get deploy rl-service -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env}'` and grepping:
```
$ kubectl -n rl get deploy rl-service -o json | jq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[] | {name, value}' | grep EXEMPTIONS_ORDER -A1
{
  "name": "EXEMPTIONS_ORDER",
  "value": "after_accounting"
}
```

luca: that matches. we also have a feature flag flip in LaunchDarkly for `rl.exemptions_v2` set to true for all prod.

hannah: I triggered the flag for canaries but not for prod. looks like the LD key was scoped incorrectly and propagated to prod groups. pushing kill-switch now.

hannah: toggling `rl.exemptions_v2` -> false in LD for prod.

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: LaunchDarkly flag change recorded (user: hannah).

maya: CS reports multiple customers seeing 429s and degraded UX on embeddings calls. CS ticket ids: CS-9881, CS-9883, CS-9890. priority customers: acme-inc, beta-saas.

ryan: after flipping LD flag I still see elevated 429s. digs into token metrics: token-accounting-rate shows double-counting spike coincident with deployment timestamp.

jin: checking logs for token counter, sample: `2026-03-15T14:02:11Z rl-handler INFO token_count=120 user=acct_123 request_id=abcd` then later `token_count=240` for same request where response is 429. looks like delta computed twice.

luca: hypothesis: the reorder change caused an extra increment path. if exemptions are evaluated after accounting we can double-increment for exempted prefixes when fallback path triggers.

hannah: ok plan: 1) temporary kill-switch at deploy layer -> set EXEMPTIONS_ORDER back to `before_accounting` via kubectl patch, 2) if not enough, rollback v2.3.7 to previous revision, 3) contact customers.

ryan: executing patch:
```
$ kubectl -n rl set env deployment/rl-service EXEMPTIONS_ORDER=before_accounting
deployment.apps/rl-service env updated
```

deploy-bot: update applied to deployment rl-service in prod by ryan.

luca: rolling restart triggered, new pods coming up. monitoring...

ryan: new pods up but 429s only partially dropped. token double-count still present in traces for some routes.

jin: safe rollback seems necessary. starting rollback to revision 41 (pre-v2.3.7).

deploy-bot: Rollout undo initiated: deployment/rl-service -> revision 41 by jin. status: in-progress.

hannah: notifying CS and support: "We're rolling back a recent deploy that introduced a rate-limit regression; expected mitigation within 10-15m. Apologies for the interruption."

maya: posting to affected customers now, flagging acme-inc as high priority.

luca: post-rollback metrics: 429s trending back to baseline ~8m after rollback completed. token accounting metrics normalized.

ryan: confirming: rollback completed at 1905378790, error rates back to normal at 1905378860.

hannah: thank you team. immediate actions: incident ticket created (INC-2026-045), severity=sev2, timeline & owners: postmortem assigned to jin, SRE follow-up by luca, mitigation code revert PR by hannah.

maya: customers updated. CS opened refund/comping workflow for impacted customers. will share list in INC.

luca: handoff — I will own the on-call for the next 12h to watch for regressions and validate canary gating before re-deploy. ry an take next shift?

ryan: yep I'll be available for questions, handing back to luca.

hannah: retro action items: - add canary prod scoping in LD review checklist, - require env guard in manifests, - add token-accounting unit tests for re-order behaviors.

jin: also will add a runtime assertion that detects double increment within a single request path. PR coming.

hannah: closing notes: incident mitigated by rollback; severity lowered to sev3 in 30m after rollback; postmortem due EOD tomorrow. great coordination, thank you. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 acknowledged and transitioned to "Stable" state.

ryan: leaving a short blameless timeline in the INC ticket now for handoff.

luca: taking over monitoring, will post any anomalies to this thread.

maya: logging customer follow-up items under INC-2026-045 -> CS notes.

hannah: everyone please add any logs or traces you saved to the incident doc.

jin: saving sample trace ids: trace-0xabc, trace-0xdef, will attach.

hannah: thanks again — closing thread for active remediation.
